title: 1985 AHSME Problem 5
statement: Which terms must be removed from the sum \[ \frac12+\frac14+\frac16+\frac18+\frac1{10}+\frac1{12} \] if the sum of the remaining terms is to equal \(1?\)

solutions.text:
The full sum is \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{\substack{60+30+20\\{}+15+12+10}}{120} &=\frac{147}{120}. \end{aligned} \] The removed terms must therefore total \(\frac{27}{120}=\frac{9}{40}.\) Since \(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{10}\) \(=\frac{5}{40}+\frac{4}{40}\) \(=\frac{9}{40},\) those are the required terms.

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Compute how much larger the full sum is than \(1\)
Use a common denominator of \(120\) to compare the candidate pairs
